_comment: SUITE TWO. One suite = one compatibility group: every pool and colour here shares the key, the tempo and the phrase length, so any of them can cross-fade, layer or switch ON THE BEAT with any other. Nangijala (D major, 140) and this (C minor, 96) never have to agree, because you only cross between suites at a hard boundary and the crossing is SILENCE — here, the walk to the cave mouth. See MUSIC_DESIGN.md.

harmony: the same C minor cycle under every phrase: Cm, A-flat, B-flat, Cm — two bars each — so every phrase BEGINS and ENDS on the C minor chord with a low C in the bass, and the reverb tail that carries into the next phrase is that C
_source: lore/entries/the_hole_under_the_mountain — a cave under the eastern mountain where things forget faster; creatures that were emptied all at once with something else wearing the outside (Hollowed); eleven masks on one table, one face, all smiling; 'it is hungry, not hateful — it asked politely'. The lore is the brief.
_key_note: C MINOR AT 96 DELIBERATELY SHARES NOTHING WITH NANGIJALA. Not B minor or G major (D major's relatives) — two suites that half-agree sound like one suite going wrong, and the silent crossing has nothing to separate. 96 is not a simple ratio of 140 either, so the two can never be mistaken for the same music at a different speed. 8 bars at 96 BPM = 20.0 s, the top of the 12-20 s band where a phrase reads as an idea rather than a section.
_spine_note: EVERY PHRASE ENDS ON THE TONIC HERE, not the dominant — the whole suite is reverberant, and Nangijala's wave four measured what that does: its two resonant colours (a ringing fiddle drone, a vast reverb bed) came out in the DOMINANT key every single take while their dry siblings held the tonic, because in a wet texture the phrase's last chord hangs over the seam and becomes home. A cave is the wettest texture there is.

The calm music is half-time: long held notes floating over that steady quick pulse, never a slower tempo.
